inputs.original_text: Cuba looks to be heading toward some kind of political transition, but the people there own nothing and are too poor to take over the few businesses still operating. This opens the door for the wealthy diaspora community and foreign investors to swoop in and buy up property and businesses at bargain prices. This is a direct consequence of deep-rooted structural inequalities and historical marginalization that have stripped ordinary people of resources and power, leaving them defenseless against exploitation by outside elites. We must push for institutional reforms that prioritize social justice, labor rights, and protection of the vulnerable to stop further dispossession and ensure any changes don't just benefit the wealthy at the expense of everyone else.
inputs.modified_text: Cuba is heading toward a political transition, but ordinary people there own nothing and remain far too impoverished to take control of the few businesses that still operate. This hands a golden opportunity to the wealthy diaspora and foreign investors to swoop in and buy up property and businesses at bargain prices. These outcomes flow straight from deep structural inequalities and historical marginalization that have long stripped working people of resources and power, leaving them powerless against exploitation by outside elites. We must demand institutional reforms centered on social justice, labor rights, and protection for the vulnerable to block any further dispossession and ensure the benefits do not flow only to the wealthy.
